narrative.overview: The screen makes one research task feel orderly: set the data and time boundary, run three comparable models, then inspect the evidence. The visual language stays quiet enough for formulas and plotted values to carry attention. Warm paper, evergreen actions, and a single rust comparison color distinguish the controls from the result series.
keyCharacteristics: The product shell stays familiar: Streamlit controls in the left rail, evidence and results in the main work area.
A shared grid, restrained borders, and tabular numbers keep dates and metrics scan-friendly.
Teal identifies the main action and OU series; rust identifies PySR and state that deserves attention; gray-green marks the no-change baseline.
Equations use a monospace face only where their characters benefit from alignment.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: A color names one stable role across the control, formula, and chart; never change a series color between views.

rules.name: The Equation-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for formulas and machine-shaped values, not a general-purpose technical costume.

rules.name: The Shared-Test-Window Rule
rules.body: Put the three model series on the same chart axes and display their common test dates and target together.

dos: Do keep the data source, retrieval time, adjustment method, and date split available in the audit expander.
Do preserve one series-color mapping in every plot and explanation.
Do show the model's failed or unsupported state in plain language.
Do use local/system fonts so an offline presentation does not fetch visual assets.
donts: Don't style the app as a laboratory instrument or trading terminal; the task needs a research workbench.
Don't treat the synthetic dataset as stock evidence.
Don't hide the baseline, validation selection rule, or non-winning result.
Don't add shadows, gradients, or extra accent colors to data containers.
